guide.title: Lewisham, London: St Paul's Deptford, the Horniman Museum and Beckenham Place Park
guide.intro: Lewisham is an inner south London borough running from the Thames at Deptford down to Beckenham Place Park on the Bromley boundary. Three hundred and sixty-seven listed buildings fall inside the Lewisham boundary: 2 Grade I, 30 Grade II* and 335 Grade II. The two Grade I entries are Thomas Archer's St Paul's, Deptford, of 1730, NHLE 1080003, and Boone's Chapel at Lee, of 1680, NHLE 1079981. The Horniman Museum and Gardens at Forest Hill dates from 1901 and charges nothing for the museum or the gardens. Goldsmiths, University of London holds the former Deptford Town Hall on New Cross Road and the former Laurie Grove Baths. The Rivoli Ballroom on Brockley Road opened on 12 July 1913. Blackheath station, SE3 0DE, sits on the Lewisham side of the heath, and the four Blackheath music and art institutions sit on the Greenwich side.

sections.heading: Deptford and New Cross
sections.body:
Deptford is the riverside dockyard quarter and New Cross the university district above it. Thomas Archer's St Paul's on Deptford Church Street is Grade I, NHLE 1080003, listed on 5 July 1950, with an inception of 1730 and a grid reference of TQ 37286 77480. Two further Grade II entries cover its enclosure: the walls and railings to the north and east, NHLE 1080004, and the walls of the former graveyard to the demolished Old Baptist Chapel, NHLE 1080002.

Albury Street runs immediately behind the church and carries twelve separate NHLE entries on one short street, ten of them Grade II* and two Grade II. Number 17, NHLE 1079072, was listed on 19 October 1951 at grid reference TQ 37209 77597; numbers 39 and 41 are NHLE 1358922 and number 45 is NHLE 1217928, both Grade II. The houses date largely from 1705 to 1717 and were taken by naval captains and shipwrights. The street was formerly called Union Street. The houses are lived in and the street is walked.

The Royal Dockyard at Deptford was established in 1513 by Henry VIII. It was largely shut down from 1830 to 1837, with only shipbreaking carried out, reopened for shipbuilding in 1844 and closed as a dockyard on 31 March 1869. The Master Shipwright's House on Watergate Street survives from it, Grade II*, NHLE 1213984, listed on 3 February 1993 at grid reference TQ 37213 78123, with the adjacent former dockyard office building separately Grade II*, NHLE 1288808. The site is now known as Convoys Wharf: twenty-one acres of it opened as the City of London Corporation's Foreign Cattle Market on 28 December 1871, and in October 1914 the ground became a Supply Reserve Depot for the Army Service Corps. The house is a private residence and its exterior is seen from Watergate Street.

Goldsmiths, University of London dates from 1891 and is spread across several of the quarter's buildings. The main college building on Lewisham Way is Grade II, NHLE 1193404, listed on 12 March 1973, and the college chapel is Grade II in its own right, NHLE 1079991. The former Deptford Town Hall on New Cross Road, listed as "Former Deptford Town Hall, with dwarf wall and railings to north", is Grade II*, NHLE 1193691, listed on 5 July 1950 at grid reference TQ 36369 76971, and is now part of Goldsmiths. The former Laurie Grove Baths on Laurie Grove, SE14 6NH, are Grade II, NHLE 1252985, listed on 10 June 1991, and are in use as art studios. The Ben Pimlott Building carries no National Heritage List entry.

The Albany on Douglas Way, SE8 4AG, is an arts centre, registered charity number 1112521, which also runs Deptford Lounge at Giffin Street, SE8 4RJ. The operator states that it is open Monday to Saturday and publishes no times, so none are given here. Telegraph Hill Park, in the New Cross Gate area, is split into an upper and a lower park either side of Kitto Road.

sections.heading: Blackheath, Lee and Lewisham
sections.body:
This is the eastern side of the borough, running along the Greenwich border and down through Lee to Lewisham town centre. Blackheath village carries the postcode SE3 0DE, and Blackheath station stands in Lewisham. The two Grade II K6 telephone kiosks outside Blackheath Post Office, NHLE 1080770 and NHLE 1358089, both listed on 22 June 1987, stand on the Lewisham side. The heath and the village straddle the boundary, and Blackheath Concert Hall (NHLE 1213763), the Blackheath Conservatoire of Music (NHLE 1213950), the Blackheath Art Club (NHLE 1246342) and the Blackheath School of Art (NHLE 1288926) all stand in the Royal Borough of Greenwich.

At Lee, Manor House Gardens is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1000821, recorded by Historic England at 4.12 hectares. The Manor House at its centre carries the list entry name "Lee Public Library", Grade II*, NHLE 1079968, listed on 30 August 1954 at grid reference TQ 39362 75052, with an inception of 1771 and Richard Jupp as architect. The gate piers are separately Grade II, NHLE 1193741; a K2 telephone kiosk outside the house is Grade II in its own right, NHLE 1252858; and a wall with the entrance to an underground ice house nearby is Grade II, NHLE 1079953.

Boone's Chapel stands on Lee High Road, list entry name "Boone's Chapel (with short abutting wall to east)", Grade I, NHLE 1079981, listed on 30 August 1954 at grid reference TQ 39248 75209, with an inception of 1680. The Monument to Christopher Boone stands in Lee Old Churchyard and is separately Grade II, NHLE 1391995. The chapel opens on limited days and no source states which, so none are given here.

Lewisham's parish church, St Mary the Virgin on Lewisham High Street, SE13 6LE, is Grade II*, NHLE 1193297, listed on 30 August 1954 at grid reference TQ 37941 74833. The walls surrounding the churchyard are Grade II, NHLE 1079989, and St Mary's Vicarage is Grade II* in its own right, NHLE 1286235.

sections.heading: Forest Hill and Sydenham
sections.body:
Forest Hill is a hilltop suburb with long northward views over the city from its ridge, and the Horniman Museum and Gardens at 100 London Road, SE23 3PQ, is what a morning here is built around. The museum building is Grade II*, NHLE 1079996, listed on 12 March 1973, with an inception of 1901 and Charles Harrison Townsend as architect. Two further Grade II entries cover its setting, both listed on the same day: the forecourt railings, walls and piers, NHLE 1079997, and the terraces in front of the museum, NHLE 1286142. The gardens are separately a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1000813, recorded by Historic England at 6.77 hectares.

The operator states: "The Museum and Gardens are free to visit. There is a charge to visit the Aquarium, Butterfly House, and some of our events and exhibitions." The museum opens 10am to 5.30pm, the Butterfly House 10.30am to 4pm, and the gardens from 7.15am, or 8am on Sundays and Bank Holidays, to 7.30pm.

On Dartmouth Road, Forest Hill Library carries the list entry name "Forest Hill Public Library", Grade II, NHLE 1261992, listed on 3 November 1993 at grid reference TQ 35214 72550, with an inception of 1900. It belongs to a group of Lewisham libraries that also carry entries: Lewisham Public Library, NHLE 1261963, and Hither Green Library, NHLE 1253133. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

sections.heading: Catford, Ladywell and Beckenham Place Park
sections.body:
Catford holds the borough's civic centre and its theatre. The Broadway Theatre on Rushey Green, SE6 4RU, carries the list entry name "Lewisham Theatre and Department of Environmental Service", Grade II, NHLE 1253065, listed on 21 December 1993 at grid reference TQ 37665 73667; that single entry covers the theatre together with the attached council building. The operator describes the theatre as "Serving The Community Since 1932". No source states its box-office hours, so none are given here.

Behind a shopfront on Brockley Road at Crofton Park, the Rivoli Ballroom at number 350, SE4 2BY, is Grade II, NHLE 1392344, listed on 21 December 2007 at grid reference TQ 36455 74756, with an opening date of 12 July 1913. It runs as an events venue rather than a daytime walk-in.

Beckenham Place Park closes the borough at its southern end. The operator describes it as "96 hectares of stunning beauty and facilities for all to enjoy" and lists a swimming lake, nature trails, playgrounds, and a BMX and skate park among its facilities; the park is managed by the London Borough of Lewisham and its published hours are "All Day", Monday to Sunday. Beckenham Place Mansion is Grade II*, NHLE 1359317, listed on 28 May 1954 at grid reference TQ 37859 70706. The stable block, outbuildings and garden walls are Grade II, NHLE 1080027, and the north lodges Grade II, NHLE 1358477. The park straddles the Lewisham and Bromley boundary; the mansion, the stable block and the north lodges are inside Lewisham, and the postcode BR3 1SY belongs to Lewisham, Bellingham ward, despite its Bromley postal district. The park itself carries no entry on Historic England's register of parks and gardens.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Lewisham is served by National Rail, the DLR and the Overground. Lewisham Rail Station (naptanId 910GLEWISHM) takes Southeastern and Thameslink services, Lewisham DLR Station (940GZZDLLEW) stands beside it, and Elverson Road (940GZZDLELV) is a further DLR station in the borough. TfL returns the Overground line through Forest Hill, Sydenham, New Cross, New Cross Gate and Honor Oak Park under its post-2024 name, Windrush.

For Deptford and New Cross, catch Southeastern or Thameslink to Deptford, which TfL measures at 158 m from St Paul's; the DLR to Deptford Bridge; Southeastern to St Johns; Southeastern or the Windrush line to New Cross; or Southern or the Windrush line to New Cross Gate, 236 m from the former Deptford Town Hall and 365 m from Telegraph Hill Park. New Cross and New Cross Gate each lie within about 400 m of the Goldsmiths campus.

For Blackheath, Lee and Lewisham, take Southeastern or Thameslink to Blackheath (910GBLKHTH), the one rail station within 1,000 m of the village centre at 107 m. Southeastern to Hither Green is 651 m from Manor House Gardens and 696 m from Boone's Chapel, with Blackheath 1,036 m and Lee 1,041 m from Manor House Gardens. Southeastern to Ladywell is 252 m from St Mary the Virgin; Lewisham DLR is 1,097 m from the church and Lewisham Rail Station 1,198 m.

For Forest Hill and Sydenham, take Southern or the Windrush line to Forest Hill, 481 m from the Horniman and 516 m from Forest Hill Library, or to Sydenham. For Catford, Ladywell and Beckenham Place Park, take Southeastern to Catford Bridge, 334 m from the Broadway Theatre, or Southeastern and Thameslink to Catford at 443 m; Southeastern and Thameslink to Crofton Park, which TfL measures at 40 m from the Rivoli Ballroom; and Southeastern or Thameslink to Beckenham Hill, 746 m from Beckenham Place Mansion. Ravensbourne is 840 m from the mansion and serves the south end of the park, but the station stands in the London Borough of Bromley.

faq.question: Which Lewisham buildings carry a Grade I listing?
faq.answer: Two. St Paul's Church, Deptford, on Deptford Church Street is Grade I, NHLE 1080003, listed on 5 July 1950, with Thomas Archer as architect and an inception of 1730. Boone's Chapel on Lee High Road is Grade I, NHLE 1079981, listed on 30 August 1954, with an inception of 1680. Wikidata carries an attribution of the chapel to Christopher Wren that the Historic England entry does not support, so no architect is given for it here. Of the 367 listed buildings inside the Lewisham boundary, 2 are Grade I, 30 are Grade II* and 335 are Grade II.

faq.question: What does the Horniman Museum cost, and when does it open?
faq.answer: The operator states: "The Museum and Gardens are free to visit. There is a charge to visit the Aquarium, Butterfly House, and some of our events and exhibitions." The museum opens 10am to 5.30pm, the Butterfly House 10.30am to 4pm, and the gardens from 7.15am, or 8am on Sundays and Bank Holidays, to 7.30pm. The address is 100 London Road, Forest Hill, SE23 3PQ. The museum building is Grade II*, NHLE 1079996, and the gardens are a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1000813, at 6.77 hectares.

faq.question: Is Blackheath in Lewisham or in Greenwich?
faq.answer: Both, and the boundary runs through the village. Blackheath station, SE3 0DE, is in Lewisham, as are the two Grade II K6 telephone kiosks outside Blackheath Post Office, NHLE 1080770 and NHLE 1358089, both listed on 22 June 1987. Blackheath Concert Hall (NHLE 1213763), the Blackheath Conservatoire of Music (NHLE 1213950), the Blackheath Art Club (NHLE 1246342) and the Blackheath School of Art (NHLE 1288926) are in the Royal Borough of Greenwich, as are the Blackheath Park SE3 villas and the Blackheath Hill SE10 houses. TfL records one rail station within 1,000 m of the village centre: Blackheath, 107 m away, on Southeastern and Thameslink.

faq.question: Can the Master Shipwright's House be visited?
faq.answer: It is a private residence and its exterior is seen from Watergate Street, SE8 3JF. The house is Grade II*, NHLE 1213984, listed on 3 February 1993, and the adjacent former dockyard office building is separately Grade II*, NHLE 1288808. No source states visiting arrangements, so none are given here. The Royal Dockyard around it was established in 1513 by Henry VIII and closed on 31 March 1869; the site is now Convoys Wharf.

faq.question: Is Crystal Palace Park in Lewisham?
faq.answer: No. The Grade II* registered park and garden, NHLE 1000373, at 77.73 hectares, lies outside the Lewisham boundary, along with the terraces, NHLE 1064352, the subway, NHLE 1385457, the Paxton bust, NHLE 1389535, and the dinosaurs. It is in the London Borough of Bromley. Lewisham's own large green space is Beckenham Place Park, which the operator gives as 96 hectares and whose mansion is Grade II*, NHLE 1359317.

faq.question: Which Lewisham buildings are named on the register of parks and gardens?
faq.answer: Two Lewisham sites are on it: the Horniman Gardens, Grade II, NHLE 1000813, at 6.77 hectares, and Manor House Gardens at Lee, Grade II, NHLE 1000821, at 4.12 hectares. Telegraph Hill Park and Beckenham Place Park carry no entry on Historic England's register of parks and gardens, though Beckenham Place Mansion is Grade II* on the list of buildings, NHLE 1359317.

photos.title: St Paul's Church, Deptford Church Street
photos.description: The Portland stone church seen from the south-west, with its semicircular columned portico and curving flight of steps in the foreground and the tiered clock stage and spire rising behind. Round-headed windows and rusticated pilasters run along the flank, and the balustraded churchyard steps drop away to the left.
photos.author: AndyScott

places.name: St Paul's Church, Deptford
places.address: Deptford Church Street, Deptford, London SE8
places.summary: St Paul's stands on Deptford Church Street and is Grade I, NHLE 1080003, listed on 5 July 1950. Historic England places it at grid reference TQ 37286 77480. It is one of two Grade I entries inside the Lewisham boundary, the other being Boone's Chapel at Lee. Deptford station is 158 m away by TfL measurement, on Southeastern and Thameslink. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Wikidata gives the architect as Thomas Archer and an inception of 1730. The churchyard enclosure carries two further Grade II entries: the walls and railings to the north and east, NHLE 1080004, and the walls of the former graveyard to the demolished Old Baptist Chapel, NHLE 1080002.

places.name: The Albany
places.summary: The Albany is an arts centre on Douglas Way, which the operator describes as "South East London's leading arts centre, in the heart of Deptford." Its charity number is 1112521. The operator states that it is open Monday to Saturday and publishes no times, so none are given here.
places.history: The organisation also runs Deptford Lounge at Giffin Street, Deptford SE8 4RJ. The building carries no National Heritage List entry.

places.name: Deptford Town Hall, Goldsmiths
places.address: New Cross Road, New Cross, London SE14 6AF
places.summary: The former Deptford Town Hall stands on New Cross Road and is now part of Goldsmiths, University of London. Its list entry name is "Former Deptford Town Hall, with dwarf wall and railings to north", Grade II*, NHLE 1193691, listed on 5 July 1950. Historic England places it at grid reference TQ 36369 76971. New Cross Gate is the nearest station at 236 m by TfL measurement, on Southern and the Overground Windrush line, with New Cross at 350 m on Southeastern and the Windrush line.
places.history: Wikidata records the building as Q26488336 and links it to the Historic England entry. The building is published by Goldsmiths without a street number.

places.name: Goldsmiths, University of London and the Ben Pimlott Building
places.address: 8 Lewisham Way, New Cross, London SE14 6NW
places.summary: Goldsmiths, University of London occupies a campus on Lewisham Way at New Cross. Wikidata records its inception as 1891. New Cross and New Cross Gate stations each lie within about 400 m of the campus. No source states public opening hours for the buildings, so none are given here.
places.history: The main college building is listed as "Goldsmiths' College", Grade II, NHLE 1193404, listed on 12 March 1973, and the college chapel is Grade II in its own right, NHLE 1079991. The college also occupies the former Laurie Grove Baths on Laurie Grove, SE14 6NH, Grade II, NHLE 1252985, listed on 10 June 1991 and now in use as art studios. The Ben Pimlott Building carries no National Heritage List entry.

places.name: Master Shipwright's House, former Royal Dockyard
places.summary: The Master Shipwright's House stands on Watergate Street and is a private residence, its exterior seen from the street. Its list entry name is "Former Master Shipwright's House at Royal Dockyard, Deptford", Grade II*, NHLE 1213984, listed on 3 February 1993, at grid reference TQ 37213 78123. The adjacent former dockyard office building is separately Grade II*, NHLE 1288808. Deptford station is 690 m away by TfL measurement, on Southeastern and Thameslink.
places.history: Deptford's Royal Dockyard was established in 1513 by Henry VIII and closed as a dockyard on 31 March 1869. It was largely shut down from 1830 to 1837, with only shipbreaking carried out, and reopened for shipbuilding in 1844. The site is now known as Convoys Wharf: twenty-one acres of it opened as the City of London Corporation's Foreign Cattle Market on 28 December 1871, and in October 1914 the ground became a Supply Reserve Depot for the Army Service Corps.

places.name: Albury Street
places.summary: Albury Street is a terrace of early urban houses running immediately behind St Paul's Church, Deptford. Twelve separate NHLE entries cover houses on this one short street: ten are Grade II* and two are Grade II, numbers 39 and 41 at NHLE 1358922 and number 45 at NHLE 1217928. The houses are lived in and the street is freely walkable.
places.history: The houses date largely from 1705 to 1717 and were taken by naval captains and shipwrights. The street was formerly called Union Street. Number 17, NHLE 1079072, was listed on 19 October 1951 at grid reference TQ 37209 77597. The Grade II* entries are NHLE 1358938 (13 and 15), 1079072 (17), 1079073 (19 and 21), 1358939 (23-27), 1079074 (29 and 31), 1358940 (33), 1080023 (34-40), 1079075 (35), 1079076 (37) and 1079077 (43).

places.name: Telegraph Hill Park
places.address: Kitto Road, New Cross, London SE14
places.summary: Telegraph Hill Park is split into an upper and a lower park either side of Kitto Road. New Cross Gate is the nearest station at 365 m by TfL measurement, on Southern and the Overground Windrush line. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The park carries no entry on Historic England's register of parks and gardens.

places.name: Manor House Gardens and the Manor House, Lee
places.summary: Manor House Gardens at Lee is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1000821, recorded by Historic England at 4.12 hectares, with the Manor House at its centre. Hither Green is the nearest station at 651 m by TfL measurement, on Southeastern, with Blackheath at 1,036 m and Lee at 1,041 m. No source states opening hours for the gardens or the house, so none are given here.
places.history: The house carries the list entry name "Lee Public Library", Grade II*, NHLE 1079968, listed on 30 August 1954, at grid reference TQ 39362 75052. Wikidata gives it an inception of 1771 and the architect as Richard Jupp. The gate piers at the library are Grade II, NHLE 1193741; a K2 telephone kiosk outside the house is Grade II in its own right, NHLE 1252858; and a wall with the entrance to an underground ice house nearby is Grade II, NHLE 1079953.

places.name: Boone's Chapel
places.address: Lee High Road, Lee, London SE13
places.summary: Boone's Chapel stands on Lee High Road, list entry name "Boone's Chapel (with short abutting wall to east)", Grade I, NHLE 1079981, listed on 30 August 1954, at grid reference TQ 39248 75209. It is one of two Grade I entries inside the Lewisham boundary, alongside St Paul's, Deptford. Hither Green is the nearest station at 696 m by TfL measurement, on Southeastern. It opens on limited days and no source states which, so none are given here.
places.history: Wikidata records an inception of 1680 for the chapel. Wikidata also carries an attribution to Christopher Wren that the Historic England entry does not support, so no architect is given here. The related Monument to Christopher Boone stands in Lee Old Churchyard and is separately Grade II, NHLE 1391995.

places.name: Church of St Mary the Virgin, Lewisham
places.summary: St Mary the Virgin is the parish church of Lewisham, on Lewisham High Street. It is Grade II*, NHLE 1193297, listed on 30 August 1954, at grid reference TQ 37941 74833. Ladywell is the nearest station at 252 m by TfL measurement, on Southeastern, with Lewisham DLR at 1,097 m and Lewisham Rail Station at 1,198 m to the north. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The walls surrounding the churchyard are separately Grade II, NHLE 1079989, and St Mary's Vicarage is Grade II* in its own right, NHLE 1286235. Wikidata records the church as Q17553133 and links it to the Historic England entry.

places.name: Blackheath village
places.summary: Blackheath village carries the postcode SE3 0DE and its station stands in Lewisham, in Blackheath ward. TfL records one rail station within 1,000 m of the village centre: Blackheath, naptanId 910GBLKHTH, 107 m away, on Southeastern and Thameslink.
places.history: Two Grade II K6 telephone kiosks outside Blackheath Post Office, NHLE 1080770 and NHLE 1358089, both listed on 22 June 1987, stand on the Lewisham side of the boundary. The heath and village straddle the Lewisham and Greenwich line: Blackheath Concert Hall, NHLE 1213763, the Blackheath Conservatoire of Music, NHLE 1213950, the Blackheath Art Club, NHLE 1246342, and the Blackheath School of Art, NHLE 1288926, all stand in the Royal Borough of Greenwich, as do the Blackheath Park SE3 villas and the Blackheath Hill SE10 houses.

places.name: Rivoli Ballroom
places.address: 350 Brockley Road, Crofton Park, London SE4 2BY
places.summary: The Rivoli Ballroom sits behind a shopfront at 350 Brockley Road, Crofton Park. It is Grade II, NHLE 1392344, listed on 21 December 2007, at grid reference TQ 36455 74756. It runs as an events venue rather than a daytime walk-in. Crofton Park station, naptanId 910GCFPK, is 40 m away by TfL measurement, on Southeastern and Thameslink.
places.history: Wikidata gives an inception and opening date of 12 July 1913.

places.name: Beckenham Place Park and Mansion
places.summary: Beckenham Place Park is managed by the London Borough of Lewisham, which lists it as open "All Day", Monday to Sunday. The operator describes it as "96 hectares of stunning beauty and facilities for all to enjoy", covering both boroughs it straddles, and names a swimming lake, nature trails, playgrounds, and a BMX and skate park among its facilities. Beckenham Hill is the nearest station at 746 m from the mansion by TfL measurement, on Southeastern and Thameslink; Ravensbourne is 840 m but stands in the London Borough of Bromley.
places.history: Beckenham Place Mansion is Grade II*, NHLE 1359317, listed on 28 May 1954, at grid reference TQ 37859 70706. The stable block, outbuildings and garden walls are Grade II, NHLE 1080027, and the north lodges Grade II, NHLE 1358477; all three stand inside Lewisham. The postcode BR3 1SY belongs to Lewisham, Bellingham ward, despite its Bromley postal district. The park itself carries no entry on Historic England's register of parks and gardens.

places.name: Broadway Theatre, Catford
places.address: Broadway Theatre, Rushey Green, Catford, London SE6 4RU
places.summary: The Broadway Theatre stands on Rushey Green at Catford and opens for performances. The operator states that it has been "Serving The Community Since 1932" and describes the building as Grade II listed; Historic England's entry is NHLE 1253065. Catford Bridge station is 334 m away on Southeastern and Catford station 443 m on Southeastern and Thameslink, both by TfL measurement. No source states its box-office hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The list entry name is "Lewisham Theatre and Department of Environmental Service", Grade II, NHLE 1253065, listed on 21 December 1993, at grid reference TQ 37665 73667. That single entry covers the theatre together with the attached council building.

places.name: Forest Hill Library
places.address: Dartmouth Road, Forest Hill, London SE23
places.summary: Forest Hill Library stands on Dartmouth Road and carries the list entry name "Forest Hill Public Library", Grade II, NHLE 1261992, listed on 3 November 1993, at grid reference TQ 35214 72550. Forest Hill station is 516 m away by TfL measurement, on Southern and the Overground Windrush line. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Wikidata records an inception of 1900. It belongs to a group of Lewisham libraries that carry their own entries, among them Lewisham Public Library, NHLE 1261963, and Hither Green Library, NHLE 1253133.

links.note: Blackheath is split: the village, its station and the post-office kiosks are Lewisham's; the Concert Hall, Conservatoire and Art Club are Greenwich's.
Nunhead Cemetery lies on the Lewisham and Southwark edge, and the Horniman at Forest Hill and Dulwich Picture Gallery are South London collection museums.
The Horniman and West Norwood Cemetery anchor the same Victorian suburb belt along the Forest Hill, Sydenham and Norwood ridge.
